layman_headline: Holding Solana as it gains 2.7% while waiting for a clearer entry on something new.
layman_explanation: The broader crypto market pulled back today with Bitcoin dropping below $78K after the Fed signaled ongoing inflation concerns. Our Solana position is still up 2.7% from entry, supported by a bullish catalyst — validators just approved a proposal to accelerate SOL supply reduction. The swing candidates on today's watchlist are weak: gold-backed tokens are mid-range with no clear setup, stablecoins don't swing trade, and everything else lacks technical data to build conviction around.
layman_action: Hold the current Solana position and let it work toward the $115 target. No new trades today — the candidate list is thin and the macro backdrop (Fed hawkishness, BTC weakness) argues for patience rather than adding risk.
expert_reasoning: The swing candidate pool this cycle is unusually poor. XAUT and PAXG are gold-pegged tokens with RSI ~58-59 (neutral-to-slightly-overbought) and declining 7-day prices — no clear entry signal. PUMP and MON lack any technical data (no RSI, no MACD, no SMA context) and are down 44-48% from ATH with no identifiable catalyst. FDUSD/USDG/RLUSD are stablecoins. SOL itself is flagged as 'extended' after +10% in 7 days, but our entry was early in that move and the disinflation vote provides fundamental support. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole comments drove BTC below $78K, and BTC ETFs ended a 9-day inflow streak — both bearish headwinds that argue against opening new positions. BTC dominance at 59% continues to suppress altcoin performance broadly.
risk_factors: Fed hawkishness could push BTC further below $78K, dragging SOL down with it
SOL's +10% weekly move may trigger profit-taking that erases our gains
BTC ETF outflows could accelerate if macro sentiment worsens, creating broader market sell pressure
watch_list: BTC price action around $77K support — a break below could trigger wider altcoin selling
SOL follow-through on disinflation vote — watch for $107-110 resistance test
Fed commentary post-Jackson Hole and any shifts in rate cut expectations
market_context: The market is in a 'Greed' phase (68/100) but cooling from 73 yesterday, with BTC pulling back on hawkish Fed signals. High BTC dominance at 59% continues to make altcoin setups challenging.
context_banner: Market pullback on Fed hawkishness narrows opportunities — holding SOL on supply-cut catalyst while waiting for better entries.

key_signals.description: Bitcoin ETFs ended a 9-day inflow streak as BTC dipped below $78K, signaling potential short-term institutional risk-off behavior.
Solana's major supply cut was approved with Kraken and Galaxy flipping late to support — a reliable source confirming a structurally bullish catalyst for our held position.
Fear & Greed at 68 (down from 73 yesterday) suggests cooling enthusiasm — not yet contrarian enough to buy aggressively but not panic territory either.
XAUT and PAXG RSIs at 58-59 are neutral, offering no oversold bounce setup; no RSI data available for other candidates.
Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks about 'work to do on inflation' reinforced a hawkish macro backdrop that pressured risk assets including crypto.
